meta.name: 3I/ATLAS
meta.note: SPHEREx caught the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS in two observing campaigns, and these 116 frames give its brightness from 0.75 to 4.95 microns.
meta.method: Per frame: a 6 arcmin cutout at IRSA's predicted comet position, a fixed 4 pixel (24.6 arcsec) radius aperture, sky from the median of a 12 to 20 pixel annulus, times the pixel solid angle to get microjanskys; error from the annulus scatter; wavelength from each frame's per-pixel wavelength map at the measured centroid. Qualitatively this can be compared with Lisse et al. (arXiv:2601.06759), the SPHEREx team's 3I/ATLAS spectrum, whose bands (water, C-H, CO2, CO) are the ones listed under bands; no numbers from that paper are used here.
caveats: The comet is an extended coma, so the flux depends on the aperture: these are 4 pixel (24.6 arcsec) radius sums with no aperture correction, and a different aperture gives a different spectrum.
This is flux, not reflectance: the solar spectrum and the changing comet-Sun and comet-SPHEREx distances are not divided out.
No water-ice claim is made from the December data.
Each frame sees one wavelength at a different time, so rotation and activity changes between frames are mixed into the spectrum along with wavelength.

The August 2025 rows come from a different date, when the comet was much fainter and farther away, so they sit 10 to 50 times lower and should be read as a separate epoch, not part of the December spectrum.
The sky annulus (12 to 20 pixels) can contain outer coma, so the fluxes may read low.
